success_patterns: All 8 passing answers had one clean object per clause, full `Provider: Endpoint` names, correct brackets, and every clause covered, including the last one. They matched narrow endpoints to each facet (Ski Weather API, Meteosource astro, Station Climate Data, SBB Autocomplete, Flixbus stations).

Required parameters came straight from the query wording: offset `0`, `type`=`weekly`, `zipcode`, `resort`, `station`, `sku`. Stated counts and defaults were also mapped, such as `limit`=`100` and Asos `country`/`lang`.

The remaining score losses were all in optional parameters, never in tool choice. A plural count was dropped ('5 chess puzzles' with no `count`). 'First 15 posts' gave `per_page` without `page`=`1`. The chess themes were sent as one string instead of a JSON array with `themesType`. A US ski resort got no imperial `units`.
Coordinates were handled two ways, and both scored. Two fields took separate `lat` and `lon`; a single-field tool took the combined string `point`=`39.48,-106.04`.

patch.reasoning: Tool choice and structure were perfect across the batch, so the remaining loss is optional-parameter completeness. The same misses repeat across several tasks: a dropped plural count, a missing page=1 next to per_page, chess themes in the wrong form, a missing locale unit, and the coordinate pair format. Each edit adds one short rule with a concrete example next to the existing parameter rules, and none restates existing text.

edits.target: 'Between X and Y', 'at least X' and 'at most Y' -> the tool's min*/max* pair when it has one.
edits.content: - FIRST-N + PAGING. When a tool has both a page field and a size field, 'first 15 pronunciation posts' -> `per_page`=`15` AND `page`=`1`. Send `page`=`1` even though it is the default. A plural count in the clause is a parameter too: '5 chess puzzles rated 1800' -> `count`=`5`, `rating`=`1800`.

`Chess Puzzles: Puzzles` with `rating`=`1500`, `count`=`1`. Several themes: '5 puzzles, rating 1800, endgame and promotion themes' -> `count`=`5`, `rating`=`1800`, `themes`=`["endgame","promotion"]` (a JSON-array string, not 'endgame promotion'), `themesType`=`ALL`.

edits.target: Copy values verbatim from the query.
edits.content: - COORDINATES. 'coordinates 39.1911, -106.8175' -> separate `lat`=`39.1911` and `lon` (or `lng`)=`-106.8175` when the schema has two fields. Use one combined string `39.48,-106.04` (no space) when the schema has a single field such as `point` or `q`. Never guess coordinates the query does not give.

- Unit systems follow the place. A US location (Breckenridge, Aspen, a US ZIP) with a units field -> the imperial value (`i`, `us`, `F`, `MPH`). A non-US place -> metric. Only do this when the tool has a unit parameter.
